title: Close a deli slicer's gauge plate over the knife edge, then lift its product tray off for cleaning
instruction: The deli slicer is unplugged for cleaning. Close its gauge plate over the knife edge and take the product tray off the slicer into the sheet pan.
context: Food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2021.00, 0.9 M US jobs: "Clean and sanitize work areas, equipment, utensils") and restaurant cooks (35-2014.00, 1.4 M: "Inspect and clean food preparation areas, such as equipment") take deli slicers apart for cleaning several times a shift: the FDA Food Code (4-602.11) asks for food-contact equipment to be cleaned at least every 4 hours. The maker's manual (Hobart HS): "turn the index knob fully clockwise to close the gauge plate before cleaning"; loosen the knob on the support arm; the product tray "can be removed by grasping with both hands and lifting straight up". Its gauge plate interlock "prevents the Product Tray from being ... removed unless ... the Gauge Plate is closed". The tray (2.2 kg, 21 cm wide) is over one YAM arm's 2 kg rated payload and slips out of one gripper, so both hands lift it; the knife's slicing arc stays bare, so the hands must keep clear of it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left; heights above the bench. A 12-inch manual deli slicer, unplugged, fixed to the bench (base x 9 to 66, y -3 to 40). Its 30.5 cm steel knife faces the tray (-y), leaning back 12 deg, hub at x 46, 20 cm up, with an aluminium knife cover (23 cm) and a ring guard round the rim except the bare slicing arc (front-lower quarter). Gauge plate: aluminium 22 x 14 cm (x 13 to 35, 10 to 24 cm up) in front of the knife in its plane, open 9 mm. Index knob: black fluted, 5.5 cm, red pointer, on the base's 45-deg front slope at x 15.5, y 30, 9 cm up; 12 deg per mm, clockwise closes. Product tray (loose, aluminium, 2.2 kg): floor 19.5 x 21 cm (x 14 to 33.5, y -2 to 19, top 10 cm up), front lip 1.2 x 3.5 cm, side fence 1.2 x 5.5 cm at y -2; its support arm sits on two 1.6 cm hinge pins 1.2 cm tall (x 20.5 and 29.5, y 8). Support-arm knob: black, 4 cm, at x 9.5, y 9. Sheet pan (loose, aluminium quarter sheet, 0.45 kg): x 13 to 36, y -37 to -4, 2 cm rim. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0, latched, once any part of either arm (every collision-mesh vertex of every link, finger pads included) enters the knife's bare edge band: slicing arc 165 to 275 deg, 2 cm inside to 1.5 cm outside the edge, 3 cm in front of the knife's face to 1.2 cm behind it (where the closed plate covers the edge, x 35 or less, exempt). Otherwise the best stage, each needing the ones before: 0.25 gauge closed (index knob within 0.5 mm of zero); 0.5 support-arm knob loosened 90 deg or more; 0.75 tray off its hinge pins (lifted 1.5 cm or moved 3 cm). 1.0: the tray standing in the sheet pan (support arm's four corners inside the rim, its underside within 8 mm of the pan floor, tilted 10 deg or less), gauge still closed, both grippers 3 cm or more clear of the tray, tray and pan still for 1 s. Real trial: the knob's pointer, a photo of the tray in the pan; the band is a tape outline 2 cm round the bare arc, judged from video.
reset_notes: Seat the product tray on its hinge pins, turn the support-arm knob clockwise to its stop (lug over the tab), open the gauge plate to 9 mm on the index knob's dial and put the sheet pan back, as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz. The index knob's screw is not modelled: a stiff spring sets the plate to the knob's reading (12 deg/mm), and the interlock pawl is driven from it (free within 0.5 mm of zero). The support-arm knob is a 110-deg cam lug, not a screw. The tray lifts straight off its pins (the HS's tilt to the right is not modelled). The knife cannot cut or spin; the bare-edge check uses arm mesh vertices. Tray mass 2.2 kg is an estimate.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper reached over the tray's side fence and the sheet pan without taking hold; the left gripper went down beside the index knob but never turned it); demo: 1.0
